messages:
maria: Quick sync: we're debating validation UX for long console forms (create-pool, org settings). Two options on the table: 1) inline-only errors with strong field highlights; 2) a persistent compact right-hand summary that lists all errors after submit. Also revisiting destructive flows1) full typed confirmation (type resource name) or 2) lightweight confirm (checkbox + brief undo). Thoughts? alex: inline-first person here. Immediate feedback removes friction for small edits. But for multi-section forms a right-hand summary is helpful after submit to surface everything at once. leah: hybrid is my vote: validate on blur inline; on submit if errors exist show a compact summary pinned on the right with anchors. Users in testing missed errors above the fold in inline-only. Summary should be keyboard navigable. sam: accessibility checklist: summary must be in the tab order and use role=\"alert\"/aria-live assertive on submit so screen readers hear the total count. Each summary item should be a real link that focuses the control and sets aria-describedby. Example: ```
\n We couldn't save 1 errors. Press Enter on an item to jump to the field.\n
``` jordan: required marker debate: ditch asterisk-only. For critical fields show inline "Required" helper text; for less critical show a faint asterisk + tooltip on hover. Avoid color-only signals. maria: +1. Also propose we standardize on bold label + subtle helper for required; this helps tests and copy clarity. alex: on destructive actions: heavy typed-confirm is safest but slows down power users. Proposal: three-tier model: low-risk: confirm modal; medium-risk: checkbox + undo toast (10s); high-risk: short typed confirm (type "DELETE"), not full resource name. leah: usability note: participants disliked typing long names; short token like "DELETE" or "REMOVE" is okay. Focus should land in the input and we should provide copy hint like "type DELETE to confirm". sam: technical accessibility: typed input must have clear aria-label, not use placeholder as only label. Undo toast needs role=\"status\" and be focusable for keyboard users. jordan: copy phrasing for summary header: prefer "We couldn't save 1 issues to fix" over generic "There are errors". More actionable. Also each error line should be one-sentence actionable guidance. maria: layout details: summary should be collapsible and float on desktop, and replace header area on mobile (no right rail on mobile). Anchors should scroll smoothly and reveal inline message. Avoid sudden layout shifts when the summary appears. alex: implementation idea: SideErrorSummary component props: errors: Array, focusTargets: Array, onAnchorClick: (id) => void, collapsed: bool. We'll keep animation small and optional. leah: testing items: keyboard nav, screen reader announce, color contrast for required markers, focus management when jumping from summary. I'll draft an a11y checklist. aria-bot: preview build: https://staging.redwood.ai/console/ux/validation-experiments - hybrid summary + short-typed-confirm enabled by feature flag. maria: action items: alex create initial SideErrorSummary PR, leah write accessibility checklist, sam add e2e assert for aria-live, jordan run 5-person hallway test Monday, I'll collate copy suggestions. Thanks! :thumbsup:
